title: Nvidia market cap sinks below US$4 tril following Huang's resignation
article:
(Nov 13): Nvidia Corp’s stock plunged at the open on Thursday, taking the chipmaker’s market capitalisation below US$4 trillion for the first time since 2025, after chief executive officer Jensen Huang resigned following the revelation of two affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy.

The shares were down as much as 14% in early trading, dropping to their lowest since June 2025, erasing as much as US$601 billion in market value. If that holds through the close, it will be the largest one-day market capitalisation wipeout for any stock ever.

The stock has shed roughly 35% from a record hit in early October, cutting its market value by US$2 trillion in a matter of week. Nvidia was the biggest company in the world just a few weeks ago, but at less than US$3.8 trillion it’s currently below Apple Inc and Microsoft Corp.

“I’ve never seen something quite like this, so we’re in new territory,” said Ted Mortonson, technology strategist at Robert W Baird & Co. “On a scale of one to 10, this is a 10.”

Huang’s ability to stay at the helm of the most important artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker has been under scrutiny since Sunday, when he admitted to a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singaporean data centre firm Megaspeed International who’s suspected of spying for China. Then on Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, citing unidentified people who worked at the company.

See also: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO

Nvidia announced Huang’s departure before the market opened on Thursday, naming chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever chairman.

The news comes ahead of Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings report next Tuesday. The company expected to show strong growth amid robust demand for AI chips, but the scandals are causing investors and analysts to flee the stock, with at least seven Wall Street firms downgrading Nvidia over the past week. Meanwhile, the cost of protecting the firm’s debt against default neared a record.

The questions surrounding Huang added to growing concerns about the strength and longevity of the AI trade overall. Quarterly results from major Nvidia customers like Alphabet Inc, Amazon.com Inc and Meta Platforms Inc underscored how investors are losing patience with big spending on AI, especially as it turns cash flows negative.

See also: Alibaba shares drop 7% as Nvidia saga triggers chip access fears

At the same time, the US midterm elections showed many voters oppose building data centres anywhere near their communities, further clouding the outlook for spending, which translates to revenue at chipmakers and other companies involved in AI infrastructure.

Nvidia is down 15% in 2026, on track for its worst year since 2022. In contrast, the Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index is up 47% this year.

title: Existing US home sales tumble to lowest level since 2010
article:
(Nov 12): US previously owned home sales fell last month to a 16-year low as a cascade of negative news on mortgage rates and inflation deterred would-be buyers.

Contract closings in October decreased 5.5% to an annualised rate of 3.75 million, according to figures released on Thursday by the National Association of Realtors (NAR).

Sales plummeted in the West to the slowest pace in data back to 1999 and hit the lowest levels in more than a decade in both the South and Midwest.

The housing market looks increasingly grim as discouraged buyers grapple with mortgage rates above 7% and stubbornly high inflation across the economy.

At the same time, the pullback in demand may eventually help to improve affordability. Separate figures this week from online marketplace Redfin showed 36% of homes that sold last month had at least one price drop, marking the highest share in the company’s data.

See also: Fed’s Hammack says more restrictive rates are needed

The active inventory of existing homes on the market continued to rise last month, even as the number of new listings weakened, Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Drew Reading said in a Nov 9 note. That also suggests price relief may be building.

“Based on the current underwhelming home sales pace at a time of consistent job growth, there could be sizable pent-up demand if mortgage rates decline,” NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun said in a statement.

See also: US mortgage rates fall for fourth week, lifting home purchases

NAR’s data show the supply of homes on the resale market increased 4.6% from a year earlier to 1.59 million, the most for any October since 2019. That represents 5.1 months of supply at the current sales pace, the highest since late 2015.

The median sales price increased 0.4% from a year ago — the smallest annual advance since February — to US$416,700.

Housing was a key component of the affordability crisis that helped sweep Democrats to power in the midterm elections. NAR’s housing affordability index, which measures whether a typical family earns enough to qualify for a mortgage for a median-priced home, decreased to the lowest level since mid-2025.

The NAR report also showed sales of existing condominiums slid to the lowest level in records back to 1999.

Separate data out on Thursday showed applications for unemployment benefits rose last week to 200,000 but held close to historically low levels.

title: Singapore’s investigations into Alice Huang and Megaspeed International
article:
1. Singapore takes seriously its reputation as a trusted international trading and business hub. We uphold the rule of law and expect all companies operating in Singapore to conduct their business honestly and in accordance with our laws. While Singapore does not enforce unilateral export controls imposed by other countries, we expect all companies operating here to take into account such regulations, including export controls, in their international business activities. Singapore does not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate other countries’ export controls through fraud or dishonest practices. Where there is evidence of breaches of Singapore law, we take firm action.

2. In February 2025, the Singapore Police Force (“SPF”) and Singapore Customs initiated an independent investigation into several companies and their key officers, including Megaspeed International Pte Ltd (“Megaspeed”), a company incorporated in Singapore, and its controllers. The suspected domestic offences pertained to potential false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers and other related offences. As noted by Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs K Shanmugam at a press conference opens in new tab) on 3 March 2025, Singapore’s investigations were not based on any request from any country or sovereign entity.

3. Alice Huang (otherwise known as Huang Le), a Hong Kong resident, was investigated for suspected involvement in the possible offences in Singapore, given her position as then-CEO, Chairperson, and one of the key controllers of Megaspeed. Huang was not based in Singapore, and was not investigated for espionage.

4. On 24 June 2025, the US Bureau of Industry and Security (“BIS”) conducted a voluntary Post-Shipment Verification (“PSV”) check at Megaspeed with Huang present. The PSV check was the first time Singapore came to know about the US’s interest in Megaspeed and Huang. On the same day, SPF also interviewed her as part of its ongoing investigations into Megaspeed. Her passport was impounded under Section 112 of the Criminal Procedure Code 2010 to secure her attendance for purposes of the ongoing investigations, since Huang was not based in Singapore.

5. The physical servers had been purchased by companies (which were under investigation) and exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market. The SPF was investigating whether the servers had subsequently been routed from Malaysia to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore. To establish the facts, SPF could not rely solely on declarations made by the companies in Singapore. It also needed to verify these against information and records in other jurisdictions, including the jurisdictions from which the servers originated and their eventual destinations. Singapore therefore sought information from the US and other destination jurisdictions, to assist with our independent investigations.

See also: Singapore arrests and charges key aide of alleged scam kingpin

6. In particular, the SPF sought information relating to Supermicro, a US-based supplier of servers, which was relevant to the SPF’s investigations. However, Supermicro provided limited cooperation. At a meeting on 7 July 2025, SPF and the Attorney-General’s Chambers (“AGC”) raised this issue with the US authorities and requested their assistance in securing the company’s cooperation. Since September 2025, SPF has repeated this request on several occasions to the US Department of Justice (“DOJ”) and the Federal Bureau of Investigations (“FBI”). Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company.

7. In February 2026, SPF, in consultation with AGC, concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated.

8. However, SPF assessed that Huang had provided information which she knew to be inaccurate to SPF in the course of investigations, to downplay her role in Megaspeed. She was issued a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country. Other cases in the past have been dealt with in a similar way. SPF returned Huang’s passport on 26 February 2026, and she departed Singapore on the same day.

See also: Vivian Balakrishnan visits Indonesia after natural gas cuts

9. SPF’s investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals are ongoing. None of the six persons have been in Singapore since investigations commenced in February 2025.

Firm action taken against entities that violate Singapore’s laws

10. Singapore is committed to upholding our reputation as a trusted and reliable business hub. We will not allow companies or individuals to misuse Singapore's business environment to engage in fraud or dishonest practices. Singapore has charged four individuals and four companies in Court between February 2025 and July 2026 for offences — including fraud by false representation in relation to the purchase of servers, with the offences carrying imprisonment terms of up to 20 years each.

11. Our approach is clear. Singapore will conduct its own investigations independently, in accordance with our laws and based on the evidence available. We will cooperate with foreign authorities where appropriate, and take firm enforcement action wherever the evidence warrants it.

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO
article:
Jensen Huang has resigned as president and CEO of Nvidia with immediate effect, the company announced on Nov 12. Huang has also stepped down from his role as a member of the board.

Colette Kress, executive vice president and CFO of Nvidia will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. According to Nvidia’s statement, the board is looking for its next CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.

“Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” says Harvey Jones, chair of the board of directors. Jones, former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys was appointed as the first chair of the board on the same day.

“She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” he adds.

The New York Times (NYT) first reported, in October 2025, that Huang had a “close relationship” with an executive from Megaspeed, a company that was already under scrutiny for allegedly selling AI chips to China. On Oct 29, the paper reported that US intelligence concluded that the executive, Alice Huang, was passing information to Beijing. On Nov 6, citing a classified US memo, NYT reported that she had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security. The Financial Times reported, on Nov 7, that the US believed the two were in a romantic relationship.

On Nov 8, Nvidia’s board said it was initiating an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their founder and CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. It added that it had “confidence” in Jensen and his leadership team. The same day, Huang emailed employees to say he owed his family and the company an apology and that he was unfaithful to his wife.

See also: Nvidia market cap sinks below US$4 tril following Huang's resignation

On Nov 10, independent members of Nvidia’s board said they had retained former acting US Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent investigation”. The same day, US President Donald Trump said that the FBI was “looking into” Huang after he admitted to the affair with Alice Huang.

On Nov 11, the media reported a second extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. The Wall Street Journal reported, on Nov 12, that Nvidia’s board could oust Huang. The board was said to have held urgent talks on the night of Nov 11 after news of the second extramarital affair.

Nvidia will report its 3Q results on Nov 17.

See also: Alibaba shares drop 7% as Nvidia saga triggers chip access fears

As at 10.42pm, shares in Nvidia are trading at US$161.35, nearly 15% down year to date.

title: Losses from reselling homes in New Zealand hit 14-year high
article:
(Nov 12): New Zealanders are losing money when they sell their homes at the highest rate in 14 years as the nation’s property market remains depressed.

Almost 16% of properties resold in the three months through September for less than their purchase price, property consultancy Cotality said on Thursday in Wellington. That’s the most since the third quarter of 2012. Properties sold at a loss were held for a median period of 4.5 years, Cotality said.

“Most buyers would not have purchased with the intention of selling again so soon, but circumstances might have worked against them, such as a family or job change, or financial strain brought on by previously sharp rises in mortgage rates,” said Kelvin Davidson, chief property economist at Cotality New Zealand.

New Zealand’s housing market is in a prolonged slump, with prices falling for a seventh straight month to the lowest since late 2020, according to Cotality data. An 11-year-high jobless rate, subdued wage growth and high living costs are squeezing homeowners which may be prompting some to sell the houses earlier than intended.

Hardest hit have been apartments owners with 48% of their homes resold at a loss, today’s report showed. That compares with 22.5% of townhouses and 13.4% of standalone dwellings.

See also: Blackstone courts Dubai’s rich in race to tap US$1 trillion market

“Apartments tend to deliver less price growth than other property types over time, so are always a little more vulnerable to losses,” said Davidson, adding that there were also fewer apartment transactions in the quarter.

To be sure, the median loss across homes resold was just NZ$60,000 while the median gain was NZ$270,000. Those homes that sold for a profit were held for a median period of 10.4 years, Cotality said.

The share of profitable sales was 84.2% in the third quarter down from peak of about 99% in 2022.

See also: An 800 mil jobs gap in the developing world fans new risks

That suggests the deterioration in resale conditions has been more gradual than after the global financial crisis when profitable resales fell from 98% in mid-2007 to 81% by early 2009, Davidson said.

“Overall, the latest figures are not a sign of a fresh collapse,” he said. “Instead, they reflect the large falls in property values already seen, with more sellers progressively just having to make a deal in softer market conditions as each quarter passes.”

title: Poundland files to delay UK insolvency as it finds a rescuer
article:
(Nov 12): Poundland is seeking more time in its battle to avoid insolvency, via a fresh legal filing on Thursday that will come as a reprieve for thousands of workers at the British discount retailer.

The clock has been ticking for Poundland since it filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators last week, buying it 10 days of breathing space from creditors and time to find a buyer to prevent it going under. The deadline was Thursday, and under intense political pressure, the company has effectively applied for the court’s approval to push back insolvency by another 10 days.

Gordon Brothers Group LLC, which bought Poundland for £1 last year, said in a statement it is in talks with three parties over the sale of the whole business, and has received offers from other retailers to take over “significant parts” of the chain. It has released funds to let Poundland continue trading, which the retailer’s board of directors confirmed in a separate statement.

“Our efforts have continuously focused on the company’s value and its people, not prioritising one over the other,” Gordon Brothers said.

Poundland’s board said the sale process is ongoing, and the company has funding to continue trading for the notice period. The extension is aimed at “identifying the best available prospects for shareholders, creditors and our people”, the board said, adding stores remain open and trading.

With about 12,000 jobs at stake, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged owner Gordon Brothers to prevent its collapse. Though Poundland’s own management says it is profitable after an uptick in recent trading, Gordon Brothers has argued finances at the company — which it bought for £1 last year — are not sustainable and remain vulnerable to a future downturn.

See also: UK PM's rejection of EU financial rules shows Brexit reset limit

Gordon Brothers has faced scrutiny over how much it could make in fees and interest in an insolvency process if Poundland is broken up. UK lawmakers have accused it of extracting millions of pounds from the retailer, as well as starving it of funds to pay suppliers ahead of the key Christmas trading season.

“Gordon Brothers refused to say it will prioritise saving jobs over and above its own financial returns,” Liam Byrne, a Labour MP and chair of the House of Commons business select committee, said in a statement after hearing testimony from the company on Wednesday.

Gordon Brothers told MPs at the hearing it had released £11 million of funding to Poundland last week, and plans to release a similar amount next week.

See also: Brits snap up hand sanitiser, canned food on stockpile advice

The filing “may have brought some breathing space, but it means little to the staff and suppliers still facing weeks of uncertainty in the run-up to Christmas,” said Freddy Khalastchi, a recovery and restructuring partner at Menzies LLP. “Every day without an agreement makes a rescue harder, as suppliers tend to tighten their terms while a retailer’s future hangs in the balance.”

Gordon Brothers sits near the front of the queue for repayment if Poundland collapses. Most of its loans are secured against the retailer’s assets, meaning proceeds from selling inventory and other assets would go to Gordon Brothers before suppliers and other unsecured creditors.

The sales process hasn’t yielded offers that matched Gordon Brothers’ expectations, Bloomberg previously reported. A £15 million bid from real estate investor Martin Property Group — £10 million of which was deferred — was about half what Gordon Brothers has been asking for.

title: Gold extends fall below US$4,000 as market watches Fed
article:
(Nov 12): Gold fell for a third day, extending its decline below US$4,000 an ounce after persistent US inflation and hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve officials reinforced expectations for a series of interest-rate hikes.

Bullion fell as much as 1.6%, taking losses over the past three sessions to about 5% at one point. Traders are fully pricing in a quarter-point increase in December, while some even see a chance of a half-point hike. Higher borrowing costs are typically a drag on gold as it doesn’t pay interest.

Gold has struggled to sustain its brief rebound above US$4,100 an ounce late last month, which came as oil prices fell and equity markets staged a cautious recovery.

Yields on two-year Treasuries, which are sensitive to near-term rate policy, have surged around 20 basis points so far this week, while a gauge of the dollar jumped almost 1% in the previous two sessions before steadying on Thursday.

The precious metal faces further downside risk amid a less favourable macro environment, potentially falling towards US$3,870 an ounce, Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, said in a note. Any upside surprise to the US producer price index due on Friday “risks extending the recent pullback” in precious metals, he added.

See also: Singapore extends GST waiver to activities related to wholesale gold transactions

Traders will be monitoring commentary by US Federal Reserve governor Michael S Barr and other central bank officials on Thursday. A day earlier, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago president Austan Goolsbee said October’s hotter-than-expected consumer inflation report was “borderline disturbing.”

Spot gold was down 1% at US$3,947.69 an ounce as of 11.17am in London, while silver fell 1% to US$51.10. Platinum and palladium also edged lower. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was steady.

title: Bitcoin retreats as Nvidia turmoil weighs on risk appetite
article:
(Nov 12): Bitcoin retreated on Thursday as renewed unease over technology stocks weighed on risk appetite, with persistent withdrawals from US spot exchange-traded funds adding to the pressure.

The original cryptocurrency fell as much as 1.6% and was trading around US$73,500 as of early morning in New York. Other cryptocurrencies also weakened along with US stock futures, which were dragged lower as concerns over leadership turmoil at Nvidia Corp weighed on the artificial intelligence trade.

The chipmaker’s shares slumped as much as 10% in late US trading on Wednesday. Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for chief executive officer Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China, Bloomberg News reported.

Bitcoin’s recovery from its 2026 low below US$58,000 in July has recently faltered. It touched a three-month low on Wednesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation increased expectations for further interest-rate hikes.

“Bitcoin is showing signs of a changing market structure, with selling pressure concentrated in derivatives while spot market activity remains comparatively resilient,” Dean Chen, an analyst at crypto exchange Bitunix, said in a note on Thursday.

Futures cumulative volume delta — a measure that tracks whether buyers or sellers are more aggressive in the futures market over time — has turned deeply negative, while open interest also declined. “Taken together, these indicators suggest that leveraged exposure is cooling, but market positioning remains mixed,” Chen said.

See also: Double-clicking on crypto exchange safeguards

Other headwinds have also been building. Democrats scored a sweeping victory in the US elections last week, handing them control of both chambers of Congress next year. That will put the legislative branch at odds with President Donald Trump’s more crypto-friendly Republican administration. Democrats made Trump’s growing crypto fortune an issue in midterm campaigns.

Flows into spot Bitcoin ETFs reversed on Oct 30, four days before the election. Since then, the funds have seen roughly US$2.5 billion in net outflows.

MSCI Inc’s decision to drop Strategy Inc, the largest corporate buyer of Bitcoin, from its global equity benchmarks has been another factor affecting the cryptocurrency, according to Caroline Mauron, co-founder of Orbit Markets.

See also: Coinbase gets final regulatory stamp for trust-bank charter

“While that decision was widely expected, it added to the febrile mood around the asset class since the midterms,” she said, referring to elections in the US. “In the short term, there is a lack of support to the downside, with the next key level to watch at US$70,000.”

title: Merck KGaA lifts outlook again on life science strength
article:
(Nov 12): Merck KGaA raised its outlook for a third time, helped by the strength of its lab-equipment division and a better-than-expected performance of its multiple sclerosis drug, which is facing generic competition.

Full-year adjusted earnings are now expected to reach as much as €6.4 billion, up from the previous upper-end forecast of €6.3 billion, the company said on Thursday. It also increased its net sales guidance for the year.

The German science group said favourable foreign-exchange effects, a strong third quarter, and its soon-to-be-completed acquisition of Bio-Techne Corp, Merck’s largest deal in more than a decade, drove its upgrade.

After multiple failed efforts to stave off patent challenges to its blockbuster MS drug Mavenclad, Merck said it now expects no sales at all in the US from November. However, this is slightly better than previous guidance that US Mavenclad sales growth would stop in August.

Shares rose as much as 3.1% on Thursday in early Frankfurt trading, reaching the highest intraday price since October 2024. The stock is up about 24% this year through Wednesday’s close.

Chief executive officer Kai Beckmann is seeking to improve performance across Merck’s three businesses: healthcare, life science and electronics. Since he took the top job in May, Beckmann has already carried out two major acquisitions to bolster its pipeline, including the US$11.3 billion purchase of life-sciences company Bio-Techne, which should complete in December, and UK biotech Silence Therapeutics plc.

See also: EU targets social media addiction and online ‘dark patterns’

Acquisitions will continue to be “an important element of our strategy” going forward, Beckmann said on a media call, adding that the focus is on technology and innovation rather than simply growth.

Merck is also pursuing workforce reductions as part of a “strategic realignment” of the businesses. Asked about the size of the reductions, chief financial officer Helene von Roeder said they aren’t on the scale recently seen in other industries, declining to be more specific.

Merck’s “healthy showing” in the life science business and a “standout” performance in the electronics unit, helped it beat expectations in the third quarter, according to Alphavalue’s analyst Abhishek Raval.

See also: Spain’s main unions hold nationwide strike over housing costs

Life sciences, Merck’s biggest division, grew in the latest quarter, boosted by process solutions, which supplies drug-making equipment. The business had previously benefitted from increased demand from customers in Asia-Pacific due to worries over supply chain disruptions related to the Middle East crisis, though the company said current customer order trends point to a softer fourth quarter.

In its healthcare unit, organic sales edged higher during the third quarter as Merck’s new rare-disease therapies helped offset stiffer competition for cancer drug Bavencio and Mavenclad. Sales of the latter declined about 25%.

Electronics, the smallest unit, posted about 13% organic sales growth. Its semiconductor solutions business grew almost 19% organically, accelerating from the previous quarter on demand for materials used in artificial intelligence (AI)-related chip production.

Asked about a slowdown in data center construction after the US midterm elections, Beckmann said AI growth extends beyond just that build out. “There’s a lot still to happen in AI,” he said, pointing to industrial and edge AI, where applications run in factories, machines and devices. “We’re not yet scratching the surface.”

The German company is unrelated to Merck & Co in the US. The two drugmakers share historical roots but have been separate since World War I.

title: BP in talks to sell stake in Brazil oil discovery to Petrobras — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): BP Plc is in talks with Petrobras to sell a stake in the Bumerangue oil block off the coast of Brazil, its biggest discovery in 25 years, according to people familiar with the matter.

Negotiations between the two oil firms are ongoing and it’s possible a deal may not materialise, according to the people, who asked not to be identified because the talks are not public.

BP declined to comment on the matter. Petroleo Brasileiro SA, as Brazil’s state-controlled company is formally known, didn’t reply to requests for comment.

Petrobras has expertise in deepwater operations and has also been developing technology to separate CO2-rich gas from oil more efficiently and at a lower cost. That could address Bumerangue’s challenges as early samples from the reservoir, located in Brazil’s Santos basin, showed high levels of carbon dioxide, which could make development complicated.

BP has said the discovery has approximately eight billion barrels of liquids in place. The company will be gathering data from an appraisal drilling campaign in the coming months conducted by Halliburton Co, according to chief executive officer Meg O’Neill. A final investment decision is not expected before 2027, she has said.

“The engineering team is working on two paths,” O’Neill said in late October on an earnings conference call. “One is looking at early production systems and what sort of opportunity might present itself to accelerate revenue from this discovery, as well as then the full field development.”

See also: Rising fuel flows through Hormuz may help ease strained market

BP notified Brazilian regulators last month of a hydrocarbon discovery in the adjacent Tupinamba block of the Santos Basin, where BP operates with a 50% working interest alongside Shell Plc. Once BP completes drilling that section of Tupinamba, O’Neill said “we will be able to move over to Bumerangue.”

Focusing on BP’s strongest upstream assets is something shareholders expect from BP’s new top boss O’Neill, the company’s first outsider CEO. The UK oil major seeks to replenish oil reserves and increase production, turning around years of underperformance. Bumerangue is an important piece of the pipeline that offers long-term promise.

Petrobras has increasingly searched for new exploration opportunities, targeting offshore basins in Brazil and overseas areas where it can apply decades of expertise in deepwater drilling and production. The company recently announced oil finds in a controversial exploration area off the coast of the Amazon rainforest.

See also: Oil extends drop as Trump says further Iran strikes unnecessary

CEO Magda Chambriard said in September that Petrobras will need to add about nine billion barrels of oil equivalent to its reserves through 2050 to maintain production levels. Output from the prolific pre-salt is expected to peak around the middle of the next decade.

title: Genting Singapore 3QFY2026 earnings down 42% y-o-y on weaker gaming revenue
article:
Genting Singapore has reported earnings of $54.7 million for its 3QFY2026, down 42% y-o-y. Revenue in the same three months ended Sept was down 13% to $566.1 million, with its key gaming revenue portion down by more than a fifth to $315 million.

The integrated resort operator blames "softer premium gaming activity", and points out that this is a trend seen across regional key markets.

On the other hand, non-gaming revenue held steady despite smaller number of hotel room nights available.

The company says that due to ongoing upgrading of its facilities, the temporary constrain on its operating capacity will stretch through this coming FY2027.

"The group is focused on capturing year-end travel and festive demand as RWS enters the final quarter of 2026.

"Alongside these near-term priorities, the group continues to advance its resort-wide renewal, reinforcing Resort World Sentosa’s position as an integrated destination and laying the foundation for long-term growth and competitiveness," says Genting Singapore, whose share price closed at 61 cents on Nov 12, down 0.81% for the day, extending a drop of 16.44% year to date.

title: HSBC plans SRTs tied to US$7 bil of US, Asian corporate loans — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): HSBC Holdings Plc is working on two significant risk transfer deals to hedge around US$7 billion ($9 billion) of large corporate loans in the US and Asia.

The London-based lender is looking to take advantage of investor appetite for the loss-absorbing instruments with a transaction tied to about US$3 billion of US loans, according to people familiar with the matter.

It is also discussing a deal linked to about A$5.8 billion of lending in the Asia-Pacific region, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

SRTs typically insure a first loss or junior tranche of a loan book, generally equivalent to between 5% and 15% of the portfolio value. Issuance has boomed in recent years, enabling mainly European and North American lenders to offload risk tied to US$1 trillion in loans and to release regulatory capital for new lending, shareholder payouts or acquisitions.

Banks are selling SRTs at a record pace this year despite recent signs that investors are demanding better terms in the face of robust supply and wider credit market volatility. Sales are on track to reach about US$45 billion, with deals hedging AI-related assets seeing particularly strong growth, according to Crescent Capital Group LP, which invests in the securities.

HSBC has overhauled its business following the appointment of CEO Georges Elhedery in September 2024, shuttering, selling or merging several business lines and cutting thousands of jobs as it looks to refocus on its core Asian markets. It is also becoming more reliant on Hong Kong after announcing a US$14 billion takeover of partly-owned Hang Seng Bank Ltd last year.

See also: Bosch to separate auto-parts unit as Chinese rivals gain ground

Other banks are adding to the SRT pipeline. Spain’s BBVA SA is finalising a deal tied to about €4 billion of loans to mid-size corporates from its Vela SRT programme, according to people familiar with the matter. It is pricing at about 725 basis points over a borrowing benchmark, the people said, asking not to be identified because the deal is private.

ING Groep NV is also on track to complete a transaction tied to €4 billion of loans to small and mid-size companies originated by its unit in Belgium, other people familiar with the matter said. The SRT will hedge a junior piece of the portfolio, equivalent to about 5% of its value.

See also: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs in AI-fuelled push to lower costs

Representatives for BBVA and Amsterdam-based ING declined to comment.

title: Alibaba shares drop 7% as Nvidia saga triggers chip access fears
article:
(Nov 12): Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) stocks tumbled on concerns that cloud operators’ access to advanced chips may face tighter US scrutiny amid the escalating espionage and leadership controversy surrounding Nvidia Corp.

Alibaba Group Holding Ltd slumped as much as 7.3%, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index lower. The Internet giant rents Nvidia chips through Singapore-based Megaspeed International, whose founder had an affair with Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang and is suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Peers across the AI ecosystem also fell, with model developers Z.AI Co and MiniMax Group Inc sliding at least 8% each.

Chinese hyperscalers face a new geopolitical overhang just as investors are taking profits ahead of next week’s earnings season, when Alibaba and Tencent Holdings Ltd are due to report September-quarter results. Access to advanced chips has been crucial for Chinese AI model developers, which have been competing with US firms for market share in coding and agentic workflows.

“Now that scrutiny is ramping up, how long that tighter enforcement lasts will pose a real challenge for Chinese cloud service providers,” said Julia Pan, an analyst for UOB Kay Hian. “They’ve been stockpiling chips since the start of the year, so they have some buffer, but R&D timelines will inevitably be postponed.”

Nvidia has spent years lobbying Washington to allow it to sell more chips to Chinese customers. Those efforts are now coming under intense scrutiny because of the allegations surrounding Megaspeed founder Alice Huang and her relationship with Nvidia’s CEO.

See also: Tencent founder rallies half of staff behind AI-native push

While Chinese chipmakers have fast caught up in their capabilities, supply remains constrained and the likes of Alibaba continue to seek Nvidia’s advanced chips to support AI and keep their vast cloud infrastructure running.

“China’s sizable grey market for restricted Nvidia GPUs has long been an open secret and a glaring loophole in US export controls,” said Chai Chaoyi, a researcher at 86Research. “A high-profile crackdown could deter major intermediaries and materially disrupt this supply.”

Beijing on Thursday urged the US not to use allegations of Chinese spying on Nvidia’s Huang to justify technology restrictions, adding that the two sides remained in contact ahead of a planned meeting between their leaders.

title: Elon Musk says it would be an honour to hire Nvidia’s Huang
article:
(Nov 12): Elon Musk said it would be an honour to hire Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang, who is at risk of being ousted following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman reportedly suspected of spying for China.

That would be an honor — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 12, 2026

Musk’s expression of support on X, in a response to a post urging him to recruit Huang, comes as Nvidia’s board meets to consider a future without its founder. Huang has been embroiled in scandal after admitting he had an affair with an alleged spy, with the crisis escalating after a New York Times report that he had a relationship with one of his direct reports.

Musk, CEO of Tesla Inc, and Huang have known each other for at least a decade, and both men joined US President Donald Trump’s high-profile visit to China earlier this year. Musk previously expressed his admiration for Huang and said he expected to continue ordering chips from Nvidia.

I am a huge admirer of Nvidia and Jensen btw. That market cap is well-deserved. SpaceX AI and Tesla expect to continue ordering Nvidia chips at scale. — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) March 19, 2026

Nvidia is a key supplier of graphics processing units to Tesla, which uses them to train artificial intelligence models for autonomous driving and robotics. Nvidia also supplies computing technology for Tesla’s driver-assistance systems, though the carmaker is developing its own chips.

See also: Adani eyes mix of equity, debt for US$2.9 bil Evos takeover — Bloomberg

title: Tencent founder rallies half of staff behind AI-native push
article:
(Nov 12): Tencent Holdings Ltd’s billionaire founder Pony Ma said he’s willing to deploy half of his troops to AI-native businesses, urging his 100,000-strong workforce to embrace an era-defining technology.

In his annual speech marking the company’s anniversary, Ma told employees this week that the industry has entered an “Age of Discovery,” comparing Tencent’s core businesses to an army and its new AI endeavours to a navy. “The army must leverage AI to maximise its efficiency, while we redeploy 50% of our personnel to the navy to support AI-native businesses,” he said, according to people with knowledge of the event.

Ma’s comments came across more as a push for all employees to harness AI, rather than a sweeping overhaul, the people said. All businesses must rethink their positioning in the AI era, with half of Tencent focusing on boosting efficiency in existing operations, while the other half explores new avenues for growth, they cited Ma as saying.

Ma, 55, also called for a nimbler corporate structure with less mid-tier management, one where individual contributors could step up, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private information.

A Tencent spokesperson didn’t respond to an emailed request for comment.

China’s most valuable company is trying to close the gap with longtime rivals ByteDance Ltd and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd in AI. At stake is its future standing against a crop of fast-rising AI-native firms from DeepSeek to Moonshot, which have propelled the country to the forefront of the global AI race. Tencent recently scored an early win in enterprise AI, with its WorkBuddy desktop assistant ascending to the lead.

See also: AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet poised to gain from Nvidia scandal

Ma, a reclusive founder who usually shuns the limelight, has stepped up to steer Tencent’s AI strategy. Following the breakout of DeepSeek’s R1 model in early 2025, he personally made the call to integrate it into Tencent’s flagship chatbot, Yuanbao. When autonomous agent framework OpenClaw swept China this year, Ma took to his social media feeds to promote Tencent’s competing variants.

Yet Yuanbao failed to challenge ByteDance’s Doubao as China’s biggest chatbot, and Tencent’s large language model development also fell behind. The setbacks prompted Ma to say at a May shareholder meeting that Tencent was aboard a “leaky ship.”

China has yet to witness the kind of AI-induced mass layoffs seen at Silicon Valley giants like Meta Platforms Inc and Amazon.com Inc. Yet Ma’s comments about resource reallocation have stoked some fears of job cuts on Chinese social media. As of June, Tencent reported 115,927 employees, up from 111,221 a year earlier.

See also: Sony bets on homegrown anime to fuel decades of future growth

It’s unclear what structural changes Tencent will pursue. Its latest companywide reorganisation took place in 2018, when it created a dedicated cloud arm that’s now the bedrock of much of its AI push. From gaming to social media and fintech, Tencent’s various departments are already experimenting with new AI businesses, and hundreds of its products have integrated its in-house Hunyuan model series.

Much of its ambitions rest on WeChat, as the ubiquitous app is testing its own native agent that can help users summarise group chats, pay bills and order deliveries.

Tencent has shed about 33% in market value this year, dropping to roughly US$470 billion as investors increasingly scrutinise the payoff of mounting AI infrastructure spending. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 18.

title: Blackstone courts Dubai’s rich in race to tap US$1 trillion market
article:
(Nov 12): Blackstone Inc’s top private wealth executives held their first-ever gathering in Dubai to court the city’s deep-pocketed investors, as the alternative asset manager seeks to expand its business across the Gulf.

The US firm pitched its range of products, including private credit and infrastructure, to an audience of more than 100 high-net-worth individuals and representatives from platforms that distribute private investments to wealthy clients and family offices at the Waldorf Astoria in the Dubai International Financial Centre.

Speakers at the Wednesday event included Farhad Karim, chief operating officer of Blackstone Private Wealth; Carlos Whitaker, president of BCRED, its flagship private credit fund for individual investors; and Greg Blank, chief executive officer of BXINFRA, its infrastructure vehicle for retail investors.

The gathering also coincided with the opening of Blackstone’s new Dubai outpost — its first dedicated private wealth office outside Zurich.

Blackstone’s push into Dubai, where the financial hub alone is home to family offices controlling more than US$1 trillion in assets, is the latest sign of the United Arab Emirates’ continued appeal to financial firms, wealth managers and family offices despite the months-long Iran war.

“The UAE has built an extraordinary position as a global finance and investment hub and is becoming an increasingly important center for wealth management,” Blackstone president and chief operating officer Jon Gray said in an emailed statement.

See also: An 800 mil jobs gap in the developing world fans new risks

Global firms including JPMorgan Chase & Co, Barclays Plc and HSBC Holdings Plc have also been expanding their wealth businesses in the Middle East despite the regional war.

“What’s happening in Dubai isn’t cyclical. It’s structural,” Blackstone’s Karim told Bloomberg News. He said money, talent, entrepreneurs and financial institutions are all moving in the same direction, making Dubai “one of the world’s great wealth capitals.”

Private capital firms and alternative asset managers are increasingly turning to wealthy individuals and family offices as institutional fundraising has slowed. Blackstone has been at the forefront of that shift, with its private wealth business managing US$330 billion, nearly a quarter of the firm’s US$1.4 trillion in assets.

See also: US loses grip on US$121 bil mobile gaming sector to China

The push hasn’t been entirely smooth. Blackstone is navigating pressures hitting many private credit firms as some investors have rushed to redeem their capital on concerns on exposure to software companies and credit quality.

The Gulf has also become a prominent dealmaking destination for Blackstone. Despite the Iran war, the firm has struck several deals in the UAE, partnering with a Dubai firm on an aircraft-leasing venture and committing US$250 million to a payments infrastructure platform in Abu Dhabi. It also joined other global firms in a US$16 billion infrastructure partnership involving Kuwait’s oil-export pipelines, the largest foreign direct investment in the country’s history.

Blackstone is also expanding its Abu Dhabi office, already its largest in the region, to support further dealmaking.

title: AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet poised to gain from Nvidia scandal
article:
(Nov 12): Nvidia Corp’s leadership turmoil is boosting potential beneficiaries, with Advanced Micro Devices Inc, Broadcom Inc and Alphabet Inc gaining after hours on bets they may win business from the chip giant.

AMD and Broadcom each rose more than 3% as Nvidia sank 9% after hours on reports its board is preparing to oust chief executive officer Jensen Huang, who led its rise to become, at one point, the world’s most valuable company. Alphabet rose 0.3% in extended trading.

The selloff followed reports about Huang’s extramarital affairs and intensified after the Wall Street Journal said the board was preparing to remove him. Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Huang.

As Nvidia confronts leadership uncertainty, rival hardware makers are gaining as investors seek continued exposure to the AI trade while hedging Nvidia-related risks. The turmoil underscores the potential for further volatility as investors assess its impact on AI development and the extent to which customers diversify their spending worldwide.

“This is where competitors like AMD, like Google Tensor Processing Units and Amazon will probably have a chance to improve their market share when it comes to that accelerator market that Nvidia dominates,” Mandeep Singh, global head of technology research at Bloomberg Intelligence, said. “There is no doubt that Nvidia won’t be as aggressive as they have been in the past two to three years when it comes to setting goals and overachieving them.”

See also: Sony bets on homegrown anime to fuel decades of future growth

Huang’s potential replacement will likely be “quite conservative” in company leadership, given the recent developments, he added.

AMD and Broadcom stand to likely gain the most if Nvidia’s leadership issues disrupt its customer relationships. AMD is Nvidia’s closest rival in AI graphics processing units and striving to loosen its grip on the market, while Broadcom has a growing role in custom AI chips and networking.

While a Nvidia leadership shakeup may push customers to rethink their reliance on a single supplier, competitors like AMD and Broadcom are already pursuing business in AI accelerators, custom silicon and networking.

See also: SoftBank shares fluctuate after US$7 bil loss on writedown

“AMD as a direct competitor, and Alphabet and Broadcom in the TPU space, are natural beneficiaries in the short term,” said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. “Huang’s scandal has raised public doubts about Nvidia’s commercial secrets and its product edge.”

Alphabet’s TPUs are custom-built for AI, while graphics processing units are multi-purpose chips originally made for gaming. TPUs can’t replace GPUs across the board, and moving AI workloads away from Nvidia is slow and costly, she added.

Alphabet announced this week plans to roll out a broader array of AI chips, aiming to capitalise on its rapid rise as a major challenger to Nvidia in a market worth hundreds of billions of dollars. The company is introducing two new variations of its TPUs.

In Taipei, MediaTek Inc, which works with Google on custom silicon, rose as much as 3.3% in Taipei on Thursday. Design houses Alchip Technologies Ltd and Global Unichip Corp both jumped more than 8% in Taipei on hopes that rising budgets will flow into custom hardware.

Nvidia’s manufacturing partners appear largely insulated from the turmoil, given they also supply its rivals. But Samsung Electronics Co may have more to gain if the uncertainty at Nvidia leads to a shake-up in supplier relationships. Samsung outperformed memory rival SK Hynix Inc by more than one percentage point, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co was little changed.

Samsung has forged increasingly close ties with AMD, Nvidia’s biggest challenger in AI chips, while SK Hynix remains Nvidia’s primary supplier of high-bandwidth memory. During AMD chief executive officer Lisa Su’s visit to Seoul in March, Samsung agreed to collaborate with the US chipmaker on next-generation AI memory and computing technologies.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“A potential leadership change at Nvidia could create a strategic opening for Samsung,” said Jung In Yun, chief executive officer at Fibonacci Asset Management Global. “If Jensen Huang were to leave, new management could reassess supplier relationships and place greater emphasis on diversifying its supply chain, giving Samsung an opportunity to deepen its partnership with Nvidia.”

Beyond the memory giants, a number of South Korean startups — including AI chipmaker FuriosaAI and Samsung-backed MangoBoost — are also seeking to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance with alternative technologies.

The scandal could also benefit Chinese companies working to replace Nvidia in their home market, as stricter export rules in the US intensify scrutiny of chip sales to China.

Any resulting tightening would provide a tailwind for local chipmakers such as Cambricon Technologies Corp, Hygon Information Technology Co and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp.

Cambricon rose as much as 13%, while Hygon and SMIC both climbed more than 5%.

China’s tech selloff began much earlier than in the US, and investors may be eyeing cheap Chinese tech stocks as a potential hedge if the US market downturn worsens, Wu said.

“But structurally, unless Chinese tech found a fix for advanced chips, I’d say it is difficult to penetrate Nvidia’s market share,” she said.

title: Another data centre halts in Australia as public backlash rises
article:
(Nov 12): A vast data centre project near Adelaide has been suspended following community opposition, at least the third Australian development to be waylaid in recent weeks as public opposition grows.

Quantum DC Pty Ltd said Thursday it paused the planning approvals programme for a proposed 1,200-megawatt hyperscale data centre in South Australia. It said it won’t submit a development application this year.

There are “significant concerns about the project from some community members”, Quantum said in a statement. The company pointed to worries over the Tungkillo development’s location, its water use and supply, energy infrastructure, and the impact on farmland.

Nextdc Ltd chief executive officer Craig Scroggie this week vowed to make communities his top priority after local backlash delayed a major data centre project in Melbourne. Stockland Corp abandoned plans for a Sydney data centre following similar opposition. Worldwide, the sites face fierce opposition over their energy and water impacts, and concerns about the environmental fallout.

Quantum also scrapped two community information sessions about Tungkillo planned for later this month, and said they’ll be replaced by a “longer-term engagement programme”. It is the company’s only project, according to its website.

title: Adani eyes mix of equity, debt for US$2.9 bil Evos takeover — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): Indian billionaire Gautam Adani’s group is set to fund as much as half of the €2.56 billion (US$2.9 billion) acquisition of Netherlands-based liquid storage operator Evos BV with equity, with the remainder through a syndicated loan, according to people familiar with the matter.

Adani Group will infuse equity up to the equivalent of $1.45 billion to fund the transaction, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. The conglomerate, controlled by India’s richest person, is also working to refinance about €1.3 billion of existing debt at Evos, the people said.

The planned debt financing would create an opportunity for global lenders as the ports-to-power company presses with its expansion overseas by acquiring Europe’s second-largest independent liquid storage company. India’s acquisition-finance market is opening up as regulatory restrictions ease with domestic banks allowed since July 1 to fund up to 75% of the value in corporate takeovers.

The overall financing strategy is expected to broadly follow the structure used in two recent large Indian outbound acquisitions, two of the people said. Tata Motors Ltd syndicated a €3.875 billion bridge loan to fund its takeover of Iveco Group’s commercial vehicle business last year, while Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd’s US$12 billion purchase of Organon & Co involved debt funding and cash infusion.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. is the sole underwriter for the Evos transaction and is providing financing commitments for up to €2.8 billion, according to a Nov 5 statement from Adani Group announcing the acquisition.

But other lenders including DBS Group Holdings Ltd., First Abu Dhabi Bank PJSC, Barclays Plc and State Bank of India are in talks to join the financing at a later stage when a formal invitation goes out, the people said. The debt package will initially take the form of a bridge loan with a tenor of about 18 months, which could later be refinanced with longer-term debt, the people said. Discussions are ongoing and the size, structure and other terms could still change, they added.

See also: Alphabet kicks off Asia bond sale as AI firms face scrutiny

A spokesperson for First Abu Dhabi Bank declined to comment, but added that the lender remains “committed to supporting our clients across the markets in which we operate and conducting our business in accordance with the highest standards of governance and regulatory compliance.”

Representatives from Adani Group, MUFG, Barclays, DBS and SBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

SBI, India’s largest lender, formed a partnership with MUFG in March to explore merger and acquisition opportunities in the country shortly after the central bank relaxed rules on local banks funding takeovers. SBI subsequently participated in financing Sun Pharma’s acquisition of Organon.

See also: Alleged Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia firestorm is in Beijing — Bloomberg

“India’s banking sector could soon be humming with more M&A deals as a privatisation push opens the door to more foreign control, with domestic bolt-ons getting a boost from more than US$120 billion of excess capital,” said Sarah Jane Mahmud, senior analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence.

The Adani Group is accelerating expansion across its businesses as part of plans to invest US$100 billion over the next few years. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization at flagship Adani Enterprises Ltd. is expected to climb to 299 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) by fiscal year ending March 2029 from 140 billion rupees in fiscal 2026, implying compound annual growth rate of 29%, according to Morgan Stanley.

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd can maintain its financials and credit quality after its acquisition of Evos, as it expands the firm’s geographic footprint into developed markets with stable operating environments and is consistent with its growth strategy, S&P Global Ratings said.

title: Asian stocks edge higher, shrug off Nvidia woes
article:
(Nov 12): Asian stocks edged higher as investors largely shrugged off a leadership crisis at Nvidia Corp that sent shares of the chipmaker at the heart of this year’s artificial intelligence (AI) boom tumbling in after-hours trading.

The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.2%, as modest gains in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan outweighed declines in Hong Kong. The advance followed a 2.3% jump in the Nasdaq 100, putting the US tech benchmark on track for its best week since May.

Optimism around AI had been fuelled by CoreWeave Inc, which surged 25% on an upbeat outlook, while OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reached US$10 billion ($12.8 billion) and Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering was said to be multiple times oversubscribed.

That enthusiasm was tested as Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 0.6% and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.3% after Nvidia tumbled about 8% in late trading.

The chipmaker is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for chief executive officer Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman reportedly suspected of spying for China, according to a person familiar with the situation.

The leadership turmoil poses a particular risk for Asian markets given the region’s central role in Nvidia’s supply chain, which includes Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc. As the dominant supplier of chips powering AI, upheaval at Nvidia risks shaking confidence in the trade that has driven much of this year’s global equity rally.

See also: Asian stocks rise on AI enthusiasm, bonds decline

“Nvidia’s latest developments could weigh on sentiment across the broader AI trade, but we see selective opportunities emerging among semiconductor companies that can offer credible second source alternatives for critical AI chips,” said Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global. “Near term, however, investor reception to Anthropic’s IPO is likely to be a more important driver of AI sentiment.”

Beyond equities, investors were also bracing for tighter US monetary policy. The dollar held its gains after climbing to an 18-month high, with traders fully pricing a quarter-point Federal Reserve hike next month and assigning a small chance of a half-point move.

Long-end Treasuries drifted higher as trading resumed after a holiday with yields on 30-year US government bonds slipping three basis points to 5.32%. Those on 10-year notes dipped one basis point briefly to 4.98%.

See also: Asian stocks climb as tech rallies, oil slips

“Volatility is likely, so a temporary safe haven bid is to be expected,” said Justin Lin, strategist at Global X ETFs.

Global benchmark Brent crude extended declines into a third day to trade 1.1% lower at around US$91.75 a barrel, with hostilities between Iran and the US remaining muted.

Elsewhere, gold held losses in early Thursday trading after hotter-than-expected US inflation and hawkish remarks from Fed officials triggered a sell-off. Bullion fell as much as 1.2% to trade below US$4,000 an ounce during US hours.

“It’s all about the continued re-pricing of the Fed,” said Jeremy Stretch, a strategist at CIBC. “A discussion of either 50-basis-point hike or an acceleration in the pace of tightening from once a quarter is now real.”
• Meta Platforms Inc’s longtime infrastructure chief will leave the company in early 2027, a major leadership change as it continues to invest hundreds of billions of dollars in AI and the data centres needed to support it.
• United Airlines Holdings Inc is moving to block third-party AI agents from booking flights and accessing customer accounts ahead of the holiday travel season, as the growing use of AI in the airline industry raises concerns about privacy.
• BHP Group has named Adrian Wood to succeed chief financial officer Vandita Pant when she steps down from the role in February next year.
• ByteDance Ltd plans the release of a Muse-like AI assistant in the coming weeks to augment its lead in AI video, a milestone event the company hopes will help close the gap with top US labs in as soon as three years.

title: Alphabet kicks off Asia bond sale as AI firms face scrutiny
article:
(Nov 12): Alphabet Inc began marketing its inaugural Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sale, testing investor interest at a time of increasing volatility for companies focused on artificial intelligence.

The Google parent set initial price guidance for its proposed two-year, five-year and 10-year Hong Kong dollar bonds at around 4.6%, 5% and 5.5%, respectively, according to a person familiar with the matter. The company is also marketing two-year, five-year, 10-year and 30-year Singapore dollar-denominated notes, with guidance around 2.75%, 3.25%, 3.65%, and 4%, the person said.

Proceeds from the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, which may include the repayment of outstanding debt. The bonds could be priced as early as Thursday, the person said.

The deal comes at a challenging moment for technology industry borrowers. Investors have become more cautious toward AI-linked assets after a broad market selloff last week fueled by concerns that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could lead to greater scrutiny of data center development and AI infrastructure spending.

The sector has also been shaken by market turmoil sparked by Nvidia Corp, the leading maker of AI chips, which has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for chief executive officer Jensen Huang. Alphabet’s fundraising effort is part of a broader push by global hyperscalers to tap new debt markets as they seek financing for AI-related projects. The company sold its first Australian dollar bonds in August and has also issued notes in Swiss francs, British pounds, Canadian dollars and Japanese yen this year.

Alphabet and other firms, including Microsoft Corp, Amazon.com Inc and Meta Platforms Inc, have been borrowing at a record pace while simultaneously committing tens of billions of dollars to build out AI capabilities.

See also: Alleged Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia firestorm is in Beijing — Bloomberg

Earlier this month, Alphabet raised €6 billion (US$6.7 billion) through a multi-tranche euro bond sale, its second offering in the currency this year. The company paid materially higher borrowing costs than in its inaugural euro deal in May as concerns over the pace of AI spending rose.

title: HSBC explores bolstering Singapore to balance China reliance — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): HSBC Holdings plc has been exploring ways to ease its reliance on China including Hong Kong and give more independence to its Singapore operations, as the bank seeks to diversify risk across its Asia business, according to people familiar with the matter.

The London-based lender, which generated about 40% of its pretax profit in the first half from Hong Kong, has internally discussed several options to give its Singapore arm greater autonomy, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing a private matter. The initiative is carried out under the name “Project Sirena”.

HSBC’s review highlights how some of the world’s largest financial groups are moving to insulate their Asian assets from mounting geopolitical risks. Singapore, bolstered by relative political stability and its standing as a premier wealth and banking hub, has emerged as a top beneficiary as firms look beyond Greater China for operational flexibility.

It comes even as chief executive officer Georges Elhedery has repeatedly voiced confidence on Hong Kong’s prospects, predicting the city would overtake Switzerland to become the world’s largest cross-border wealth hub by the end of the decade even before it happened late last year.

In a first step, HSBC plans to combine its major banking services in Singapore under one entity over the next few years. A possible next move would be to bring in the other regional operations under the Singapore subsidiary, with the ultimate goal of establishing a second regional base alongside Hong Kong, according to the people.

In a statement, Surendra Rosha, co-CEO of Asia and the Middle East, confirmed the bank will combine its separate units in Singapore as part of a simplification drive, though said it had no further plans after that.

See also: Despite missing estimates, UOB’s Asean strategy remains intact

“All of our Asia-Pacific banking entities remain under the ownership and management of the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited subsidiary head officed in Hong Kong, and there is no plan to make any changes to this,” Rosha said in an e-mailed statement.

The deliberations remain fluid with no firm decisions on the path forward, the people said. Like other multinationals, HSBC is also wary of appearing to hedge its bets given its significant exposure in Greater China and concerns about provoking regulators, the people said. HSBC shares fell as much as 0.8% in early Hong Kong trading.

Making its Singapore operations more independent would be a major step for the 161-year-old lender, which was founded in Hong Kong and moved its headquarters to London in 1993. At the same time, the bank is becoming more reliant on the Chinese territory after last year announcing a US$14 billion ($18 billion) takeover of partly owned Hang Seng Bank, while it also has exited businesses in Europe and the Americas.

See also: It’s business as usual for DBS barring hit to trading income

Any signs of hedging Hong Kong, where HSBC serves as one of three currency-issuing lenders, would face stiff local pushback. It would also risk alienating Beijing, where the bank maintains expansive mainland operations.

HSBC’s assessment isn’t without precedent. In 2019, smaller rival Standard Chartered plc consolidated its operations into a locally incorporated subsidiary, creating dual hubs in Singapore and Hong Kong to simplify its network and trim costs.

HSBC has recently faced intense scrutiny on other fronts from Hong Kong authorities over its allocation of AI talent to Singapore as both Asian financial hubs battle for dominance.

Currently, the lender operates a hybrid structure in jurisdictions such as Singapore. In May 2016, HSBC locally incorporated its retail banking and wealth management business in Singapore under HSBC Bank (Singapore) Ltd while also operating a branch under Hong Kong. It runs locally incorporated subsidiaries in countries such as Malaysia and Indonesia, though both remain under its Hong Kong-based business.

A subsidiary is more free standing than a branch, with its own governance, capital needs and deeper local regulatory oversight. Such a structure also faces different treatment in the event of financial difficulties.

The lender has over the past couple of years radically overhauled its business following the appointment of CEO Elhedery in September 2024. Under his leadership the bank has shuttered, sold or merged several business lines, cutting thousands of jobs as it looks to refocus its operations on its core Asian markets.

Elhedery has made stripping complexity out of HSBC a central plank of his overhaul, saying earlier this year that he had been “ruthless about killing complexity” at the lender.

Hong Kong remains HSBC’s profit engine, generating US$7.8 billion of pretax profits in the first half of 2026, about 40% of the group total. Singapore, despite its growing importance as an Asian wealth hub, generated just US$774 million — roughly a 10th of Hong Kong’s profit. India contributed US$965 million and mainland China US$1.8 billion, according to HSBC’s accounts.

title: Alleged Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia firestorm is in Beijing — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 12): The suspected Chinese spy at the heart of a scandal that threatens to take down Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang has returned to her home country, people familiar with the matter said.

Megaspeed International founder Alice Huang is currently living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, one of the people said, asking to remain anonymous to discuss a sensitive situation. It wasn’t immediately clear when or why she travelled to the capital, nor what she may be engaged in, the people said.

Alice Huang’s whereabouts have been the topic of intense speculation since Nvidia’s founder admitted to an extra-marital affair and the company’s board began an investigation into allegations she’s a Chinese spy. Known also as Huang Le, the former journalist who became a power broker renting advanced chips to the nation’s top firms was the catalyst for a controversy that roiled markets and may now result in Jensen Huang’s ouster. Beijing has denied that the woman was a spy. China’s Foreign Ministry didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Alice Huang first came into the CEO’s orbit after founding Megaspeed, the largest buyer of Nvidia’s chips in Southeast Asia — a major route for smuggling the firm’s advanced hardware into China. She oversaw the incredible ascent of a fledgling neocloud, which rose to become one of Nvidia’s most important partners in the regional data centre boom. Attempts to reach her were unsuccessful on Thursday.

Online posts and publicly available information have provided the broad contours of Megaspeed’s rise, and the critical role she played in that. She founded Megaspeed in 2023 following a career in private equity and television. The company was spun off from one of China’s largest video game enterprises, 7Road Holdings Ltd, just months after former US president Joe Biden imposed sweeping restrictions on shipments of advanced AI chips to China. 7Road first sold its Singapore subsidiary to a British Virgin Islands entity called Huang Le Ltd, and Huang Le assumed control.

See also: ANZ CEO Matos warns of global jobs crisis without AI rules

In November 2023, Huang Le Ltd sold Megaspeed to a Singapore shell company. Days after the sale, the firm was designated an official Nvidia Cloud Partner — a highly coveted status that granted it preferred chip access from a company that plays kingmaker to the industry.

Trade records show that Megaspeed has since imported goods worth more than a thousand times its cash balance in 2023. Its imports of Nvidia products have topped US$4.6 billion. At multiple facilities in Southeast Asia, the company rents Nvidia chips to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, itself a recent subject of US national security concerns. The AI and e-commerce company, which has denied Washington’s allegations of ties to China’s military, has declined to comment on the relationship.Alice Huang got her start in finance before getting into the neocloud business. She served as vice general manager of Shanghai Hexi Investment Co since November 2015, the fund house said in a few posts on its official WeChat account in late 2016 and early 2017. Previously, she held roles at Citic Securities Co and HSBC Holdings Plc, according to Hexi posts.

HSBC and Citic Securities representatives didn’t respond to Bloomberg requests for comment, while Hexi wasn’t immediately available when reached by phone.

title: ANZ CEO Matos warns of global jobs crisis without AI rules
article:
(Nov 12): ANZ Group Holdings Ltd chief executive officer Nuno Matos has called for global regulation to manage the impact of artificial intelligence on the labour market, which he warned could trigger an international crisis.

Should large-scale job cuts of up to 50% emerge, “we’ll have a crisis and it’s not going to be in Australia, it’s going to be a global crisis,” Matos said Thursday during a parliamentary hearing in Canberra. “This is one of the few examples where I would say some global regulation is needed to make sure that society does not go into trouble,” he said.

The adoption of AI among Australia’s banks in recent years has coincided with job cuts amid a challenging economic backdrop. Skeptics including Australia’s finance sector union have accused banks of replacing staff with AI. Outside the finance sector, Canva Inc. this month announced a sweeping overhaul that will see 22% of its staff leave while Microsoft Corp is offering buyouts to around a quarter of its 223,000 staff as part of the tech giant’s efforts to retool its workforce for the AI era.

“I hope that obviously the world and the administrations are capable of cooperating and ensuring that this technology does not create a social problem at a global level,” Matos said.

Matos said workers should develop AI skills to reduce the risk of losing their job to colleagues who are more proficient, and pointed to ANZ’s efforts to develop staff capacity internally.The comments intensify concerns Matos has previously voiced about the quickly developing technology, which he believes could be used to attack banks as key choke-points for the economy.

“AI has a dark side,” he said. “Wide adoption of AI without having the adequate guardrails — it’s a big problem. No banks should be building AI without building the right controls,” he said, adding that ANZ is developing its own “control platform” as it employs the technology across the bank.

See also: Nintendo sold 5.2 mil copies of ‘Zelda’ remake in four days

ANZ is also using AI to prevent fraud and identify cyber weaknesses, he said.

title: StarHub’s 3QFY2026 earnings fall to $3.9 mil despite revenue growth
article:
StarHub has reported earnings of $3.9 million for its 3QFY2026 ended Sept 30, compared with $22.1 million a year earlier on a basis excluding Ensign, as higher costs weighed on an improvement in revenue.

It reiterates its guidance for a full-year dividend of at least 6 Singapore cents a share. Its policy provides for a higher payout if distributing at least 80% of earnings adjusted for one-off, non-recurring items exceeds that amount.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (ebitda) fell 26.3% to $72.1 million. Operating expenses rose 11% to $481.6 million, with the company citing higher staff costs from investments in capabilities and business growth.

Lower gross profit and other income also weighed on ebitda, while higher depreciation and amortisation hurt net earnings. Service ebitda margin narrowed to 16.8% from 23.1%.

Service revenue increased 2.9% from a year earlier and 5.2% from the preceding quarter to $396.1 million, supported by enterprise growth. Total revenue rose 4.5% to $486.8 million.

The improvement in quarterly sales came as StarHub continued to face price competition in its consumer business and sought to turn a growing enterprise orderbook into revenue.

See also: Centurion Corp’s 3QFY2026 revenue up 41% y-o-y to $95.2 mil

Enterprise revenue rose to $172.5 million from $145.6 million a year earlier. Its orderbook was 45% higher at the end of September, with the company reporting progress in delivering contracted work.

Managed services revenue increased 27.7% to $101.3 million, helped by project delivery and the timing of revenue recognition. StarHub says it aims to build recurring revenue by adding managed services to existing connectivity accounts and securing multi-year contracts.

Consumer revenue remained under pressure. Mobile revenue fell 6% to $121.2 million, broadband declined 4.1% to $57.9 million and entertainment dropped 10.6% to $44.6 million.

See also: NTT DC REIT’s 1HFY2027 DPU exceeds IPO estimate by 10%

Blended mobile average revenue per user (ARPU) fell to $19.20 from $21.70 a year earlier and $19.70 in the preceding quarter. Broadband ARPU declined to $31.90 from $34.10 a year earlier.

StarHub says it saw early signs of quarter-on-quarter stabilisation in mobile and broadband. It is seeking to restore profitable consumer growth through better customer service and differentiated offerings.

The company announced plans on Oct 8 to acquire MyRepublic’s mobile business, extending its strategy of using multiple brands to serve different customer segments through its network.

StarHub also confirms continuing discussions with Keppel over a possible transaction involving M1. However, there is no certainty the talks will lead to a deal.

Cybersecurity remains a priority, with platform investments nearing completion. The company plans to incorporate cybersecurity across its customer offerings.

For 9MFY2026, service revenue fell 3.6% to $1.14 billion and ebitda declined 24.6% to $230.7 million on an Ensign-excluded basis.

Nine-month profit was $262 million. That period includes a first-half one-off gain from the termination of an arrangement involving Ensign, after which the cybersecurity business became an associate.

Third-quarter free cash flow fell 79% to $26 million. Nine-month free cash flow was $66.3 million, compared with an outflow of $48.2 million a year earlier.

Cash balances stood at $479 million at the end of September. Net debt to trailing 12-month ebitda, excluding spectrum payments, rose to 2.76 times from 2 times at the end of 2025.

StarHub maintains its full-year ebitda outlook at 75% to 80% of the previous year’s level, equivalent to a decline of 20% to 25%. Capital expenditure commitments are expected to be 13% to 15% of total revenue, excluding spectrum rights.

The company says it has achieved about 15% of its $70 million cost savings target through 2028. The programme includes simplifying the business, optimising its network, redesigning systems and retiring older infrastructure.

title: US stocks climb as Wall Street gets fresh AI fuel
article:
(Nov 12) : A rally in tech giants lifted stocks on bets the artificial-intelligence trade that has powered the bull market has more room to run.

The revival of AI wagers sent the Nasdaq 100 up 2.3%, putting the gauge on track for its best week since May. The S&P 500 added 1.3%. Nvidia Corp. rose. CoreWeave Inc. jumped 25% on an upbeat outlook. More evidence of demand came from OpenAI, whose quarterly revenue hit US$10 billion, while Anthropic PBC’s IPO was said to be oversubscribed. European shares hit all-time highs.

The tech rebound eased concerns over whether Anthropic’s initial public offering would get done or not, said Matt Maley at Miller Tabak. A delay would have raised questions about whether the “AI bubble” was bursting, he noted.

With equities bouncing — and the “flight to safety” trade fading — Maley says fixed-income investors could be facing some renewed volatility for a while after recent economic data.

While cash trading in Treasuries was closed for Veterans’ Day, futures edged lower as the latest inflation report cemented wagers on Federal Reserve rate hikes. The dollar hit its highest since May 2025. Oil rose as traders weighed mixed signals on the prospects for an end to the Iran war.

The past week has served as a masterclass in how rapidly narratives can change in periods of heightened emotion, according to Mark Hackett at Nationwide.

See also: US stocks rise as CoreWeave outlook, Anthropic revive AI trade

While investors focus on AI uncertainty and inflationary pressure, there are several notable tailwinds that act as ballast, including a strong and steady macro backdrop, historic earnings growth, seasonal tailwinds and a complete reset of expectations, valuations and investor positioning, he added.

“This has kept the market in a prolonged trading range despite an aggressive momentum and AI selloff,” said Hackett. “If that skepticism cools, the bulls will have a distinct advantage moving forward.”

The AI-investment theme remains intact, although capital spending and profit growth among many key industry players are likely to moderate over the coming year as the buildout matures, noted Brock Weimer at Edward Jones.

See also: Nvidia’s bull case hinges on CEO Huang surviving China spy probe

“We continue to favor US large-cap stocks, which we believe offer attractive exposure to the AI theme and trade at a discount to their 10-year average forward price-to-earnings multiple,” he said. His firm also favors mid-cap shares, which would benefit from economic strength.
